# Compatibility matrix

<!-- This page is generated by scripts/compat_matrix.py from the driver tests and the pinned examples. Do not edit it. -->

Netdryrun reads each network OS through a driver. A driver is only as good as the device output it was built and tested on, so this page lists, for every driver, the exact image it is verified on, the date its test data was last captured from a live lab, and what each check does on it. It is generated from the tests (`tests/test_driver_matrix.py`) and from the images the shipped examples pin; if a cell is not on this page, it is not tested.

## Verified images

| Platform | Image verified on | Source of the image | Test data last captured live | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FRR | `quay.io/frrouting/frr:10.4.1` | Public image (quay.io). | 2026-10-28 | released |
| Nokia SR Linux | `ghcr.io/nokia/srlinux:26.7.2` | Public image (ghcr.io). | 2026-10-27 | released |
| SONiC | `docker-sonic-vs:master.1258173-c10162df4` | From the SONiC project's CI build server; contains FRR 10.7.1. Pinned by build id. | 2026-10-28 | released |
| Arista EOS (bring your own cEOS image) | `ceos:4.36.3M` | Bring your own image (free from arista.com, cannot be redistributed). | 2026-10-28 | released |
| Cisco NX-OS (beta, bring your own Nexus 9000v image) | `vrnetlab/cisco_n9kv:9300-10.4.8.M` | Bring your own image (the Nexus 9000v qcow2 from cisco.com, built with vrnetlab; cannot be redistributed). | 2026-10-30 | beta |
| MikroTik RouterOS 7 (beta, bring your own CHR image) | `vrnetlab/mikrotik_routeros:7.23.8` | Bring your own image (the CHR VMDK from mikrotik.com, built with vrnetlab; cannot be redistributed; one CHR node per lab until MikroTik confirms more). | 2026-10-30 | beta |

Every shipped example pins its image, so a new NOS release shows up as a deliberate change with re-captured test data, never as a silent change under the tests. `scripts/capture_fixtures.sh` captures the test data again from the pinned images, and `scripts/fixture_shape.py` reports any change in shape. A different image or version may work; it is not verified until it appears here.

## Check types

Each cell counts the tests on that driver's own captured output: a *must-fail* test is a violation that has to end the check as failed, a *control* is the same output without the violation, which has to pass (so a must-fail test cannot pass only because a capture no longer parses).

| Check type | FRR | SR Linux | SONiC | Arista EOS | Cisco NX-OS (beta) | MikroTik RouterOS (beta) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bgp_session` | verified (2 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (2 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (2 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (2 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (3 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (3 must-fail, 1 control) |
| `bgp_prefixes` | verified (8 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (5 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (8 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (5 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (6 must-fail, 2 controls) | verified (4 must-fail, 2 controls) |
| `route` | verified (4 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (3 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (4 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (3 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (5 must-fail, 2 controls) | verified (5 must-fail, 3 controls) |
| `bgp_route` | verified (5 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (4 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (4 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (4 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (10 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (7 must-fail, 3 controls) |
| `ping` | verified (2 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (2 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (2 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (2 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (4 must-fail, 1 control) | verified (2 must-fail, 1 control) |

## BGP prefix counts by address family

| Address family | FRR | SR Linux | SONiC | Arista EOS | Cisco NX-OS (beta) | MikroTik RouterOS (beta) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ipv4-unicast` | verified (4 must-fail) | verified (4 must-fail) | verified (4 must-fail) | verified (4 must-fail) | verified (4 must-fail) | verified (4 must-fail) |
| `ipv6-unicast` | verified (2 must-fail) | verified (1 must-fail) | verified (2 must-fail) | verified (1 must-fail) | verified (2 must-fail) | refused: not supported |
| `evpn` | verified (2 must-fail) | refused: no per-family prefix counter: a count would read 0, which passes `max` and `exact: 0` | verified (2 must-fail) | refused: no per-family prefix counter: a count would read 0, which passes `max` and `exact: 0` | refused: no per-family prefix counter: a count would read 0, which passes `max` and `exact: 0` | refused: no per-family prefix counter: a count would read 0, which passes `max` and `exact: 0` |

A check on a refused address family stops the run before the lab is deployed, with a message that names the driver. It is never run and never read as zero.

## Known limits

- **SR Linux:** `bgp_prefixes` counts the neighbor's `received-routes`, which on SR Linux 26.7.2 includes routes that fail BGP loop detection and are not usable. On a live capture of `examples/srl-frr` on 2026-10-28 the counter read 3 where one prefix was usable and `rejected-routes` read 0. A `min` or `exact` prefix check on SR Linux can pass on a count that includes unusable routes. The test data above predates that capture; it has not yet been re-captured. Mitigation: pair the count with `route` checks for the prefixes that matter. Fix scheduled: 0.4.
- **SR Linux:** graceful restart: a stale path (a restarting peer's route, kept until it re-sends it or the stale timer ends) counts as present and best; no stale marker is read yet. A route check can pass on a route that is about to go. Mitigation: leave graceful restart off in the lab, or use a `timeout` above the stale timer. Fix scheduled: 0.4.
- **SR Linux:** startup config: a line the NOS rejects at boot isn't detected yet, so the lab can run without it. Config applied with `setup:` commands is checked. Mitigation: add a positive check for what each changed line creates. Fix scheduled: 0.4.
- **SONiC:** graceful restart: a stale path (a restarting peer's route, kept until it re-sends it or the stale timer ends) counts as present and best; no stale marker is read yet. A route check can pass on a route that is about to go. Mitigation: leave graceful restart off in the lab, or use a `timeout` above the stale timer. Fix scheduled: 0.4.
- **SONiC:** startup config: a line the NOS rejects at boot isn't detected yet, so the lab can run without it. Config applied with `setup:` commands is checked. Mitigation: add a positive check for what each changed line creates. Fix scheduled: 0.4.
- **Arista EOS:** graceful restart: a stale path (a restarting peer's route, kept until it re-sends it or the stale timer ends) counts as present and best; no stale marker is read yet. A route check can pass on a route that is about to go. Mitigation: leave graceful restart off in the lab, or use a `timeout` above the stale timer. Fix scheduled: 0.4.
- **Arista EOS:** startup config: a line the NOS rejects at boot isn't detected yet, so the lab can run without it. Config applied with `setup:` commands is checked. Mitigation: add a positive check for what each changed line creates. Fix scheduled: 0.4.
- **Cisco NX-OS (beta):** Each NX-OS node is a VM inside its container: NX-API answered 5 to 7 minutes after deploy in our runs, and the node needs KVM, 4 vCPUs and about 9 GiB of memory (8 GB for the VM). Give checks a `timeout` of at least 900 s.
- **Cisco NX-OS (beta):** Failure scenarios (`link_down`, `node_isolated`) on an NX-OS node are refused: the container's interfaces only carry frames to the VM. Take the link down on the other side of the link.
- **Cisco NX-OS (beta):** graceful restart: a stale path (a restarting peer's route, kept until it re-sends it or the stale timer ends) counts as present and best; no stale marker is read yet. A route check can pass on a route that is about to go. Mitigation: leave graceful restart off in the lab, or use a `timeout` above the stale timer. Fix scheduled: 0.4.
- **Cisco NX-OS (beta):** startup config: a line the NOS rejects at boot isn't detected yet, so the lab can run without it. Mitigation: add a positive check for what each changed line creates. Fix scheduled: 0.4.
- **MikroTik RouterOS (beta):** Each RouterOS node is a VM inside its container: the REST API answers about a minute after deploy, and the startup config is imported after that (an import stops at its first error), so give checks a `timeout` of at least 600 s. One CHR node per lab until MikroTik confirms more are allowed.
- **MikroTik RouterOS (beta):** IPv6 sessions and routes, ping inside a VRF, and failure scenarios (`link_down`, `node_isolated`) are refused with a clear message, not answered.
- **MikroTik RouterOS (beta):** `bgp_prefixes` counts prefixes the router received AND policy accepted (derived from the routing route table): the session's own `prefix-count` includes rejected prefixes and is not used.
- **MikroTik RouterOS (beta):** A path without a LOCAL_PREF attribute reports local_pref as unknown, never as the default: a `local_pref` check on it fails.
- **MikroTik RouterOS (beta):** graceful restart, add-path, multipath and max-prefix behaviour are not captured yet: a route row with a key the parser does not know stops the read with an error.

## How a platform gets on this page

A driver is added when it is built from captured live output, has a must-fail test and a control for every check type, has a capture script (`scripts/capture_fixtures.sh`) and passes the same release gate as the others. A driver that is not yet proven in use is marked beta here until outside users confirm it.
